lines: Nine rooms of a people who left no name for themselves, and one honest card at the door.
I would rather this museum said I DO NOT KNOW nine hundred times
than said one clever thing that turned out to be a guess.
Free tours, and I do the Aurelian rooms because nobody else wants to.
You cannot end a tour of them. There is no ending. They simply stop.
I finish by asking the children what they think happened and I never argue.
I copy the accession pages so scholars do not have to handle them.
This hand is a pleasure to work from. Small, patient, never crossed out.
Eleven years of it and then nothing, mid-page, in the spring of 1052.
The empty case at the end is the one people ask about.
ON LOAN, eleven years, no return date, and I have never seen a loan card
with no borrower's name on it before or since.
Miss says the doors in the drowned street are all open because
the card says it might not mean anything.
But if it might not mean anything, why did they put it on the card?
One vertebra. That size. And the card will not name it.
Either they do not know, which is frightening,
or they do, which is worse. I come back every month to see if it has changed.
Eleven species in grey on that wall and two painted back in this year.
Both of those were the Foundation's breeding programme. I will say that anywhere.
They are also the ones who have not answered a letter of mine since spring.
